thirtySecondSummary: Sustainable Development assesses the balance between human socioeconomic progress and the long-term ecological preservation of the planetary biosphere.

Brundtland Commission (1987): 'Our Common Future' defined sustainable development as development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 2030): 17 global goals and 169 targets adopted by the UN in 2015 (SDG 1: No Poverty, SDG 3: Good Health, SDG 4: Quality Education, SDG 5: Gender Equality, SDG 7: Clean Energy, SDG 13: Climate Action).
Renewable Energy & Panchamrit Targets: India's commitments at COP26 Glasgow: 500 GW non-fossil energy capacity by 2030, 50% energy from renewables, and Net-Zero carbon emissions by 2070.
Green Hydrogen & Solar Alliances: International Solar Alliance (ISA - headquartered in Gurugram, India); National Green Hydrogen Mission targeting 5 MMT annual production by 2030.

coreConcepts.title: The Brundtland Definition and the 3 Pillars of Sustainability
coreConcepts.explanation:
The theoretical architecture of sustainable development rests on three interdependent dimensions:
1. Origin & Definition: Coined by the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED) chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland in the 1987 landmark report 'Our Common Future':
  - 'Sustainable development is development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.'
2. The Triple Bottom Line (3Ps - People, Planet, Profit):
  - Social Equity (People): Fair access to health, education, gender equality, and poverty eradication.
  - Environmental Protection (Planet): Conserving natural capital, preserving biodiversity, and reducing greenhouse emissions.
  - Economic Viability (Profit): Equitable wealth creation and efficient resource utilization without predatory exploitation.
keyTakeaways: Inter-generational equity: Securing resources for future generations.
Three pillars: Social, Environmental, Economic (People, Planet, Profit).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: NCERT Economics & Geography Class XII, Sustainable Resource Planning, pp. 1-25.

coreConcepts.title: United Nations 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 2030)
coreConcepts.explanation:
Adopted at the 2015 UN General Assembly under Agenda 2030, replacing the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs):
- SDG 1: No Poverty
- SDG 2: Zero Hunger
- SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being
- SDG 4: Quality Education
- SDG 5: Gender Equality
- SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation
- SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy
- SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
- SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure
- SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities
- SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities
- SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production
- SDG 13: Climate Action
- SDG 14: Life Below Water (Marine ecosystems)
- SDG 15: Life on Land (Terrestrial ecosystems)
- SDG 16: Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions
- SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals.
keyTakeaways: SDG 4 = Quality Education; SDG 5 = Gender Equality.
SDG 7 = Clean Energy; SDG 13 = Climate Action.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: CUET General Test Annual Review, UN Agenda 2030 & SDGs, pp. 740-754.

coreConcepts.title: India's Climate Commitments (Panchamrit) and Clean Energy Transition
coreConcepts.explanation:
National roadmaps driving decarbonization:
1. Panchamrit Pledge (Announced at COP26 Glasgow by India):
  - 1. Reach 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030.
  - 2. Fulfill 50% of energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030.
  - 3. Reduce total projected carbon emissions by 1 billion tonnes from now until 2030.
  - 4. Reduce carbon intensity of GDP by 45% by 2030 (over 2005 levels).
  - 5. Achieve Net-Zero carbon emissions by 2070.
2. International Solar Alliance (ISA):
  - Joint initiative launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris (2015).
  - Headquartered at the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) in Gurugram, Haryana.
3. National Green Hydrogen Mission:
  - Approved by Union Cabinet with an outlay of ₹19,744 crore; aims to produce at least 5 MMT (Million Metric Tonnes) of green hydrogen per annum by 2030.
keyTakeaways: 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity target by 2030.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, National Energy Transition Roadmaps, pp. 24-52.

workedExamples.question: By which year has India pledged to achieve Net-Zero carbon emissions under its 'Panchamrit' climate action commitments announced at COP26 in Glasgow?
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Recall the Panchamrit five-point climate pledge announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the UNFCCC COP26 summit in Glasgow (2021).

Step 2: The five pledges include: 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, 50% energy from renewables by 2030, reduction of 1 billion tonnes carbon emissions by 2030, 45% reduction in carbon intensity of GDP by 2030.
Step 3: The final long-term target is reaching net-zero carbon emissions by the year 2070.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: 2070 is a landmark target year frequently asked in CUET General Test current affairs and environmental literacy.

workedExamples.question: Where is the global headquarters of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) located?
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was jointly founded by India and France in 2015 during the COP21 Paris summit.
Step 2: It is dedicated to mobilizing investments in solar energy technologies across sunshine countries between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.
Step 3: Its interim and permanent secretariat is housed at the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) campus in Gurugram, Haryana, India.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: ISA is the first major international treaty body based in India, making it a favorite CUET GK topic.

practiceQuestions.question: The foundational concept of 'Sustainable Development' was officially defined in 1987 in which landmark UN report?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED), headed by Gro Harlem Brundtland, published 'Our Common Future' in 1987, articulating the modern definition of sustainable development.

practiceQuestions.question: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by the United Nations General Assembly under Agenda 2030?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The UN 2030 Agenda consists of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and 169 associated targets adopted in September 2015.

practiceQuestions.question: Which UN Sustainable Development Goal is specifically dedicated to 'Climate Action'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: SDG 13 urges urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. SDG 7 is Affordable and Clean Energy, and SDG 15 is Life on Land.

practiceQuestions.question: What is India's non-fossil fuel energy capacity target by the year 2030 as pledged under the Panchamrit framework?
practiceQuestions.explanation: At COP26, India enhanced its clean energy ambition to install 500 gigawatts (GW) of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was jointly conceived by India and France in 2015.
Reason (R): Its headquarters is established in Gurugram, India, to mobilize over USD 1 trillion of investments in solar energy by 2030.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both statements are true facts regarding the ISA, though (R) provides its headquarters and investment mandate rather than explaining why it was co-founded.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (UN SDG) with List-II (Core Goal):
(P) SDG 1 — 1. No Poverty
(Q) SDG 4 — 2. Quality Education
(R) SDG 5 — 3. Gender Equality
(S) SDG 7 — 4. Affordable and Clean Energy
practiceQuestions.explanation: Direct mapping of foundational UN Sustainable Development Goals.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the annual green hydrogen production target by 2030 envisioned under the National Green Hydrogen Mission of India?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to build green hydrogen production capacity of at least 5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) per annum by 2030.

practiceQuestions.question: The 'Triple Bottom Line' framework in sustainability refers to balancing:
practiceQuestions.explanation: John Elkington introduced the 'Triple Bottom Line' framework asserting that corporations and societies must measure success across three bottom lines: Social (People), Ecological (Planet), and Economic (Profit).

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following is considered a 'greenhouse gas' primarily responsible for anthropogenic global warming?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO2), along with methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and fluorinated gases, traps outgoing infrared radiation, driving the enhanced greenhouse effect.

practiceQuestions.question: The target deadline set by the United Nations for achieving all 17 Sustainable Development Goals is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Agenda 2030 establishes the target deadline of 2030 for fulfilling the 17 SDGs adopted in 2015.
